individual.label: Individual AI User
individual.intro: For one person assessing their own AI confidence, workflow, value, and responsible use.

questions.text: I understand which tasks AI is useful for in my daily work.
I can write clear prompts and improve them when the first result is weak.
I know when to use AI and when human judgment is more appropriate.
I use AI regularly for repeatable tasks, not only for experimentation.
I use AI to improve speed, quality, creativity, or problem-solving.
I have a personal process for reviewing and improving AI outputs.
I can identify the time, quality, or other benefit AI creates for me.
I compare AI-assisted results with how I worked before using AI.
I can describe at least one AI use case that has made a meaningful difference.
I know what personal, confidential, customer, or company information must not be entered into AI tools.
I verify important AI-generated facts, recommendations, code, or content before using them.
I understand the need for human judgment, attribution, and responsible AI use.

criticalRisks.text: I have entered confidential, personal, customer, or company information into an AI tool without approval.
criticalRisks.action: Stop that workflow and confirm approved tools and information-handling rules.

criticalRisks.text: I have shared or submitted AI-generated work without checking accuracy, suitability, or attribution.
criticalRisks.action: Use a verification checklist before submitting or sharing AI-assisted work.

criticalRisks.text: I use AI outputs as final decisions for important matters without appropriate human judgment.
criticalRisks.action: Keep human review and accountability for important decisions.

criticalRisks.text: I use AI tools that are not approved for my work or knowingly bypass applicable policy.
criticalRisks.action: Stop the use case and move it to an approved, compliant workflow.

company.label: Company / Team
company.intro: For a team, business unit, or organization assessing adoption, workflow integration, measurable value, and responsible capability.

questions.text: People in our team use AI tools in their regular work.
AI is available to the people who could benefit from it.
Leaders actively encourage practical and responsible AI adoption.
AI is built into repeatable workflows, not just one-off experiments.
AI improves speed, quality, customer experience, or employee experience in real work.
Teams redesign processes when AI creates a better way to work.
We define success measures before scaling an AI use case.
We track measurable benefits such as time, quality, cost, or experience.
Leaders can explain which AI initiatives are creating value.
People understand privacy, security, and responsible-use expectations for AI.
People receive practical training or coaching to use AI well.
AI outputs are reviewed with appropriate human judgment.

criticalRisks.text: Sensitive or confidential information is entered into unapproved AI tools.
criticalRisks.action: Stop the affected use case and confirm approved AI tools before continuing.

criticalRisks.text: Important customer, employee, financial, legal, safety, or compliance decisions are made from AI outputs without human review.
criticalRisks.action: Add an accountable human approval step before important decisions.

criticalRisks.text: No person is accountable for approving, monitoring, reviewing, or correcting the AI use case.
criticalRisks.action: Assign one accountable owner and define escalation and stop conditions.

criticalRisks.text: The team cannot identify a baseline, target, or measurable outcome for the AI use case.
criticalRisks.action: Define one measurable outcome and baseline before scaling.

criticalRisks.text: AI outputs are routinely used without checking accuracy, sources, or suitability.
